placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_lake_franklin, the block's Lake Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_blk_lake_franklin_d5_01, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Lake Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on Lake Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 2 printings, 1835-08-08 to 1835-08-12, claims chicago_american_1835_08_08#c001, chicago_democrat_1835_08_12#c004 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF'S PLATTED LOT FACES Lake Street, which is the plat's own answer to which street it fronts. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

citations.citation: The Chicago American. Vol. I, No. 1 (June 8, 1835) through Vol. I, No. 12 (August 29, 1835). Chicago, Ill.: T. O. Davis. Thirteen issues, OCR-assisted research transcriptions from page scans.
what_it_supplies: a second, independent contemporary witness to the town in the twelve weeks around the scene date
advertisements and self-reported addresses from a different advertiser base than the Democrat's
attestation that needs no survival liberty: the whole run is within twelve weeks of 1835-07-01
corroboration or contradiction of a Democrat address, which is worth more than either paper alone
the paper's own correction of its first masthead date
what_it_does_not_supply: any building's form, material, storey count, fenestration or dimensions
a reliable reading of a dense body column — this run had no reconciled second pass
a word count or uncertainty-marker count: none was delivered, and corpus.json records null rather than zero
identification by volume and number: No. 12 is printed on two different issues
anything at all from an engraving — the cuts are the printer's stock
a citation without an issue page and column

citations.citation: The Chicago Democrat. Vol. I, No. 1 (November 26, 1833) through Vol. II, No. 18 (August 26, 1835). Chicago, Ill.: John Calhoun, editor and publisher. Seventy-three issues, OCR-assisted research transcriptions from page scans.
what_it_supplies: that a named trade was being carried on in Chicago in a named week, and often where
self-reported addresses, which are the strongest address evidence this project has: the advertiser was paying, and his customers had to find him
dissolution, removal and replacement notices — the only thing that keeps a documented business out of the 1835 town under the owner's ruling 3
post-office letter lists, naming residents by the hundred (ruling 1: a listed name mints a resident candidate, flagged letter_list_only)
the village and later town ordinances, printed complete — the 7 November 1833 code is the richest single item in the run
arrivals and clearances, which date the piers and the harbour as working structures
public notices that fix a building as a polling place, an auction site or a meeting place on a given day
the paper's own imprint, self-reported: the corner of South Water and Clark streets
twenty-one months of continuous weekly attestation ending three weeks before the scene date, including the issue printed on 1835-07-01
what_it_does_not_supply: any building's form, material, storey count, fenestration or dimensions — an advertisement describes a trade, not a building
the specific corner of any junction it names: 'on the corner of' does not say which of the four
anything at all from an engraving — see trap 1; the cuts are the printer's stock
proof that a business named in 1833 or 1834 still stood on 1835-07-01; that is ruling 3's survival liberty, and it is a liberty
an argument from silence, unless corpus.json shows the issues either side of the silence are both in the deposit
a reading that outranks a scan read of the same passage — see ruling 2 and the C. & I. HARMON case
a citation without an issue page and column

frontage.why: T-0028, the block programme's own ticket, and the first block it has opened since 2026-08-23 — the run that day found no block left to open and filed the street control (T-0163) that was blocking them. This one needed no new control: it has stood `open` in the schedule with two free lots throughout, and what changed is the DEAL. Until T-0213 weighted the trade families onto the business front on 2026-08-26 this block was dealt I3, which tools/generate_block_infill.py refuses by name, alongside F3; T-0188 read that pair on 2026-08-27 and recorded that the block 'cannot carry a three-unit run as dealt'. Re-derived today with tools/reconcile_665.py the deal is A1, D1, D5 and F3, so three of the four are buildable and the block opens. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py lake randolph franklin wells — and on the committed dataset Lake carries 16 documented records and 8 inferred households within 25 m of its centreline against Randolph's 7 and 7. The reconstruction column is this programme's own output and does not vote. Lake is this block's business face by the town's own record, so the free Lake lot takes the row and the free Randolph lot is left open. THE END RULE IS T-A11'S, READ ON THIS BLOCK: the Dearborn Street drawbridge — the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — stands EAST of this block, so the town-centre end of the frontage is the east one, and the run is anchored there and graded that way: the deep-plan frame cottage at the east end and the older log dwelling west of it. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs away from are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. This face carried no frontage record before this run — tools/measure_street_line.py listed eight block faces and this was not one of them — so there was no built line to adopt under T-0104 and the margin is the whole of the rule. THE ONE READING THE FACE ALREADY CARRIED AGREES WITH IT, and it is worth recording because nothing made it: temple_lake_st_building, a documented record that declares no frontage and was placed by another parcel entirely, stands with its front wall 1.492 m off this face at 75.73-82.52 m along. The run this parcel builds stands at 1.499 m, 7 mm outside it, and stops 3.90 m short of it along the face. So the Lake face of this block reads as one street line rather than two, which is the defect T-0104 exists to prevent, and it reads that way because the plat module's margin and a building nobody aligned to it happen to agree — not because this run adopted anything. Lot 4 is an interior lot and not a corner one, so the standard's third clause, that a corner lot builds to the corner, has nothing to bind here; the run stands off both of its own side lines by that same margin.
